personas.drop: none (attention dips 8-11, held by the Salesforce corner tag)
personas.why: AI plus gym plus a Salesforce job tease is squarely his feed. The ghost overlay holds him past 3 s and the garden-leave line makes him send it to a batchmate. He will not comment FORM because it promises him nothing.
The red/green ghost and STOP stamp are clear and hold him through the countdown. 'Five steps' signals a tech lecture and the Salesforce tag is not his world, so he scrolls.

personas.drop: 9 (if she stays, she watches to the end)
personas.why: The corner tag about Salesforce hiring is professional gossip for an HR exec in Bengaluru, and the garden-leave line is a send to her HR group. The wave and rep-maths beats are where she is most likely to leave before the payoff.
The opening is visually understandable and the Desi Boyz beat is familiar, so he gets through the blast. Joints, waves and judges mean nothing to him and nothing in the reel speaks to his life.
She does not do reverse crunches and '122° vs 53°' is abstract to her. The countdown feels like an ad starting, so she leaves before the explanation begins.

A final-year BTech student sees a buildable project, a clean five-step architecture to save, and a real job posting at the end. The 'next: how to get it' line earns a follow, though the lead-level title is far above him and slightly weakens the pull.
The hook and the 'wall of 23 sets' data visual suit an analyst, and he likely gyms. By step three the pace feels like a list with two more items to go, and the job is not relevant to finance.
He appreciates the '23 sets, one STOP' precision and the sourced 'reportedly' framing if he reaches it. At 10 pm he has little patience for a numbered explainer and leaves once the steps begin.
Layoff news and an AI job in Bengaluru are directly relevant to a Big 4 analyst worried about his own role. He stays for the tag payoff and sends the ending, but does not save the architecture.
He likes the 'two AIs must agree' idea as a governance point and the false-alarm twist is a good story. 'So who checks my AI?' answers itself for him, and he leaves before the Salesforce ending.

He watches as a practitioner and rates the craft: frame-one visual, planted loop, re-hook at two-thirds, comment trigger. He notes the comment ask has no deliverable and that the ending belongs to a different reel, so he does not engage himself.
The ghost overlay is a strong visual and the countdown has energy. The reel then turns into a product walkthrough with no benefit for her, and she scrolls.

The judge-versus-coach cross-check and the honest false positive are what a backend dev respects, and the diagram is a save. He is mildly sceptical of the Salesforce tease as bait because the role is model training, not this pipeline.

The refusal to judge when a joint is hidden, the personal baseline and the camera-angle failure are credible engineering details. The LLM post-training posting is his exact job market, so he sends it. He finds the countdown slightly cringe.

'Legs swinging. Abs not lifting.' is his language and the ghost overlay is something he would show a client, so he may send it early. The tech steps lose him, and he has an unanswered question about why a short reverse crunch deserves a STOP rather than a correction.
The beat and the red STOP stamp buy a few seconds. There is no joke, no relatable person and no payoff for a BCom student, and the job at the end is out of reach.

top_fixes: State the physical stake in the first 10 seconds: one on-screen line saying what the swung reps cost (for example, the lower back doing the work instead of the abs). At present 'the set I should never have done' never says why, which is the main reason mass viewers leave by beat 7.

Use the lunge clip as the running example in every step visual (joints lock on the lunge, the wave is the lunge knee, the baseline is the best lunge rep), so the five steps play as one story heading to the false alarm instead of a numbered list. This targets the drop at beats 8-11.

Make the corner tag carry the tension for non-builders: change it to something like 'AT THE END: LAYOFF NEWS + THE AI JOB REPLACING IT' in wording FACTS supports, and pulse it once around beat 10. The garden-leave angle is what holds HR, consulting and finance viewers, and they do not learn of it until beat 22.

Give the comment trigger a concrete return, such as 'Comment FORM + your lift, I'll run the most-asked one next', and move 'SAVE THIS' onto its own clean hold of the full diagram. Without a deliverable, almost no persona comments.

Bridge the gym tool to the job in beat 21 with a true link, for example 'Checking an AI's mistakes is the skill here', as on-screen text only. Without it, the Salesforce ending reads as a separate reel to marketers and builders, and the lead-level title feels out of reach for students.
